cards: S05 — The Protégé Problem | S53 — I Made You Ready
reason: Both claim another performer’s competence as proof of the holder’s teaching and continuing seniority.
recommended_action: Keep S05 as the broad Core engine; rewrite S53 around succession, independence, or loss of influence.

cards: S10 — Old Rivals | S202 — Permanent Scoreboard
reason: Both turn nearly every event into points on an ongoing rivalry scoreboard.
recommended_action: Keep S10; give S202 a consequence or rule for how the remembered score changes present choices.

cards: S11 — Only You | S83 — My First Call
reason: Both make one person the holder’s primary trusted resource while concealing dependence.
recommended_action: Keep S11; rewrite S83 around reflexive first contact or habit without repeating the trust/dependence engine.

cards: S12 — After What Happened | S108 — The Feeling Never Left
reason: Both keep an old hurt emotionally present and filter current offers through it.
recommended_action: Keep S12; make S108 use a distinct trigger, coping behavior, or attempted repair pattern.

cards: S16 — For Their Own Good | S208 — I Decide What You Can Risk
reason: Both control another person’s choices while framing that control as protection from consequences.
recommended_action: Keep S16; rewrite S208 around unequal risk, consent to risk, or who bears consequences.

cards: S24 — The Grand Design | S144 — Everything Connects
reason: Both interpret coincidences, interruptions, and doubt as evidence of one larger hidden design.
recommended_action: Keep S24; rewrite S144 around testing competing explanations or managing information rather than broad pattern certainty.

cards: S28 — Regular Around Here | S172 — Knows the Customs
reason: Both perform insider status through routines or unwritten rules while hiding uncertainty.
recommended_action: Keep S28; rewrite S172 so the holder enforces or translates customs rather than pretending familiarity.

cards: S73 — Emotional Seniority | S77 — Older in This Relationship
reason: Both claim superior authority to interpret a relationship because of emotional seniority or longer memory.
recommended_action: Keep S73; rewrite S77 around archival memory, precedent, or generational rank without claiming the same interpretive authority.

cards: S122 — Authority by Bluff | S218 — One Detail Could Undo Me
reason: Both project control while fearing that one question or recurring detail will expose how little authority they possess.
recommended_action: Keep S122; make S218 about a detail that reverses status or changes meaning rather than merely exposing a bluff.

cards: S148 — Obviously One of Us | S161 — I Get the Joke
reason: Both overaccept bizarre developments to prove belonging while concealing confusion.
recommended_action: Keep S148; rewrite S161 around social timing, shared humor, or joining a pattern rather than generic belonging-through-acceptance.

cards: S168 — The Universe Is Rhyming | S240 — Everything Rhymes Eventually
reason: Both treat repeated words, shapes, or actions as rhyming evidence of one grand pattern.
recommended_action: Keep S168; rewrite S240 around callbacks changing consequence or relationship meaning, not another cosmic pattern.

cards: S35 — You Know the System | S179 — I Need Your Access
reason: Both rely on another person’s system knowledge or access while resisting the influence created by that dependence.
recommended_action: Keep S35; rewrite S179 around gatekeeping, sponsorship, or permission rather than navigational dependence.

cards: S59 — Indispensable Rival | S203 — The Rival I Need
reason: Both need a rival’s judgment or presence in order to sharpen performance while denying the dependence.
recommended_action: Keep S59; rewrite S203 around mutual escalation, identity, or fear of winning without the rival.

cards: D26 — One Last Thing | D218 — One More Unresolved Reason
reason: Both prevent departure by producing one more unresolved reason whenever the previous reason ends.
recommended_action: Keep D26; make D218 reopen an earlier reason with changed meaning rather than simply adding another.

cards: D07 — Join Me | D127 — Join the Inner Circle
reason: Both recruit someone into a secret plan; the latter mainly adds exclusivity and partial information.
recommended_action: Keep D07; rewrite D127 around recruiting a specific function such as witness, decoy, gatekeeper, or keeper of the secret.

cards: D13 — Helpful Culprit | D133 — The Helpful Suspect
reason: Both hide responsibility for causing the problem while eagerly organizing its investigation.
recommended_action: Keep D13; rewrite D133 around steering suspicion, controlling evidence, or protecting a second culprit.

cards: D16 — Confess First | D136 — Confess Before I Do
reason: Both maneuver another person into confessing before the holder reveals anything.
recommended_action: Keep D16; rewrite D136 around eliciting motive, exchanging partial admissions, or confirming a theory.

cards: D19 — Everything Is a Contest | D211 — Turn It into a Tiebreaker
reason: Both turn every disagreement into another competition meant to settle who is better or right.
recommended_action: Keep D19; rewrite D211 around formal rematches, score rules, or consequences of a tie.

cards: D36 — Hand It Over | D60 — Yield Control
reason: Both make another person surrender control of a task, decision, resource, or authority symbol.
recommended_action: Keep D36; rewrite D60 around a public transfer of legitimacy, delegation, or ceremonial yielding.

cards: D50 — Not Dismissed | D170 — You Haven’t Been Dismissed
reason: Both keep someone present by treating departure as something that requires the holder’s permission or completion of a final formality.
recommended_action: Keep D50; rewrite D170 around jointly completing a ritual or acknowledging a transition rather than permission to leave.

cards: D59 — Obey Without Explanation | D155 — Prove You Accept the Premise | D179 — Follow the Custom
reason: All use increasingly inconvenient demands or formalities as tests of obedience, belief, or respect.
recommended_action: Keep D59; redesign D155 and D179 so one tests enacted belief and the other tests interpretive respect without repeating escalating inconvenience.

cards: D135 — A Kinder Version | D159 — A Kinder Impossible Truth
reason: Both protect someone with a kinder, edited version of a harsher truth; the impossible framing is mostly cosmetic.
recommended_action: Keep D135; rewrite D159 around sustaining impossible hope through practical actions or evidence rather than another kinder lie.

cards: D137 — Exactly as Planned | D161 — That Was Phase One
reason: Both treat every failure as a necessary phase proving that the plan is proceeding exactly as intended.
recommended_action: Keep D137; rewrite D161 so failure changes the goal, reveals a new rule, or creates a distinct next phase.
